gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-arimo: Arimo reads like a tidy plain sans with a tall mean line and rounded shapes that stay open at the ends. Stencilia above it is the structural, striking one. Over many lines the body would feel steady.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-armata: Stencilia is the striking one here, a display face with stencil-like gaps in its curves and a tight band between x-height and ascenders. Armata, in sans-serif form, does the quieter job, spacing its letters generously.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-athiti: Athiti reads friendly and contemporary in sans-serif form, with a high mean line and a see-through gap in each s. Stencilia brings the structural punch with pinched joints, while Athiti keeps its ends smooth and unflared.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-atkinson-hyperle: Stencilia's spacious curve gaps beside a compact band under the ascenders give it a cut-stencil, structural look. Atkinson Hyperlegible, a plain sans, follows with clipped capitals and wide-set terminals on s.

Approachable is how Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono feels, with clipped capitals and counters that breathe into the white space. Stencilia grabs attention with structural, striking curves, while the mono body in sans-serif form simply keeps spacing wide open.
Big-eyed lowercase, rounds left unlatched. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next is the sans-serif body, so a heading in Stencilia could go large while the body stays modest.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-blinker: Blinker reads friendly and clean, with open apertures. Stencilia's gappy stencil ends give structure on top, and Blinker's stroke ends look cut from one ribbon beneath.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-carrois-gothic: Carrois Gothic brings a modern, professional sans with a high x-height and a generous opening in c. Carrois Gothic would crowd Stencilia if the heading were made small, since the display face needs room.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-carrois-gothic-s: Approachable and contemporary, Carrois Gothic SC keeps a clear opening at every curve end. Stencilia is best at structural, striking display shapes, while the plain sans body is best at staying quiet, with capitals barely taller than lowercase.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-chivo: Tight lowercase, bright curves. Stencilia does best at striking, structural display work, while Chivo, the sans-serif body, does best at professional, approachable text with daylight in every opening.
